# GameObjects options

6 options. Set them in the daemon's `.conf` file or `appsettings.json`. Full reference: [configuration.md](../configuration.md). All areas: [index](README.md).

Daemon says which server reads it. Reload says whether `.reload config` applies it: `live` is applied to the running server, `restart` keeps its value until the next start, `start` is read once when the daemon starts.

## `GameObjects`

| Option | Type | Default | Allowed | Daemon | Reload | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `LootSettlementBudgetSeconds` | `int` | `15` | a whole number, -2147483648 to 2147483647 | World | start | Seconds one dungeon chest loot settlement may take end to end (the taker's save, the instance write drain, the loot transaction) before it is abandoned: a take that never started is refused to the client as usual, one whose outcome cannot be read kicks the taker. Operational, not a gameplay rule: 15 is the shipped value, three typical lock waits of the shipped 5 s Database:SqliteWriteTimeoutMs in a row (an unrelated character's write already in flight on the character save queue's one consumer, the taker's own save, the loot transaction), so one locked write ahead of it cannot use up the budget. A write-gate wait is not capped at one bound: it gives up after 5 s without a hand-off or 20 s of active waiting, but the settlement's budget token ends any wait it is passed to earlier. Valid range 1-300. |
| `MiningAmountRate` | `float` | `1` | a number, '.' is the decimal point | World | start | vmangos Rate.Mining.Amount (CONFIG_FLOAT_RATE_MINING_AMOUNT, default 1; LootHandler.cpp:455-457): scales the minimum and maximum number of opens of a multi-use mineral vein (chest.minSuccessOpens / maxSuccessOpens). Default 1 (retail). |
| `MiningNextRate` | `float` | `1` | a number, '.' is the decimal point | World | start | vmangos Rate.Mining.Next (CONFIG_FLOAT_RATE_MINING_NEXT, default 1; LootHandler.cpp:466-474): scales the chance that a mineral vein past its minimum opens stays for one more open. Default 1 (retail). |
| `PersistRespawn` | `bool` | `true` | true \| false | World | start | `GameObjects:PersistRespawn`: despawned database spawns keep their respawn time across restarts (vmangos `gameobject_respawn`, characters database; the counterpart of `Creatures:Respawn:Persist`). False keeps the timers in memory only, as before the table existed. |
| `RandomRespawn` | `bool` | `true` | true \| false | World | start | vmangos GameObjectData::GetRandomRespawnTime (GameObject.cpp:706-709): the respawn delay of a database spawn is a random value between spawntimesecsmin and spawntimesecsmax. False always uses the minimum. |
| `TransportAnimationDbcPath` | `string` | `null` | text | World | start | A build-5875 TransportAnimation.dbc (vmangos loads it with the other DBCs): the animations of the elevators and trams (type 11), whose create block then carries the progress through their cycle. Empty (the default): their progress stays 0, as vmangos without the data. |
